messages.subject: Likert type inventory scoring
parts:
Hi Phil. 
As known, when CTT are used, we use 1-2-3-4-- (values of likert choices) used for scoring of likert type questions and, if the one dimensional model is confirmed, you could also sum up factor scores to obtain total inventory score. 
As you already cited in different topics, when mirt frame is preferred, the situation become complicated. 
I had an inventory measuring emotional intelligence with 3 dimensions. Theoretically factor scores could be summed to obtain total score whict is already confirmed in CTT perspective. Now I want to convert scoring system totally to IRT perspective. I spesifically wonder whether or not is it possible to obtain values of likert choices from item parameters to use in obtaining total scores

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Likert type inventory scoring
parts:
If your test contains a simple structure where each dimension loads on only one item then making subtest total scores is fairly justified. If there are cross-loadings, however, I would not advise this as the meaning of the sum score can be misleading. It's somewhat justified if you have some structure like a bifactor, but even here the sum scores would ignore the residual dependencies caused by the distinct factor components, so paradoxical behaviour could arise.

Phil
